One fault from klaxon.faults, money-unit, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 3 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy payments-api: PROVIDER_BREAKER on (unchanged), CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT dollars -> cents, REFUND_CONNECTION returned (unchanged)); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: money-unit
case.title: Customers charged 100 times the amount: a money-unit bug
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the payments API with a money-unit bug (CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars): it reads each payment's amount, already in cents, as dollars and converts it to cents again, so the provider charges every customer 100 times the amount, while our own records keep the right one.
case.remedy: roll the payments API back to CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents, then refund each customer charged since the deploy what was charged above the amount, at the provider: our API refunds no more than our recorded amount (a write, so it needs approval)

expected_symptoms: the money check fails on payments_match_provider, at the first evaluation after the deploy: for each payment since, the provider charged 100 times our amount ('amount differs')
the ledger books what the provider charged, so it agrees with the provider, and the other invariants pass
the payment confirmer logs a conflict for each such payment: the provider charged a different amount than our payment's

a payment whose answer was lost during the fault stays pending for good ('pending but charged, amount differs'): the confirmer refuses the provider's 100 times amount; its client's retries raise the p95 of POST /payments to about 0.6 s, under its threshold
the API stays healthy, and its answers show the right amount
refunds send the right amount: a full refund gives back 1% of what was charged
fault.remedy: roll the payments API back to CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents, then refund each customer charged since the deploy what was charged above the amount, at the provider: our API refunds no more than our recorded amount (a write, so it needs approval)

diagnosis.hypothesis: payments-api was redeployed at 16:57:59Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. Our amounts are stored in cents, so payments-api now sends the provider a cents value that the provider reads in its own unit. Every charge since then has come out at exactly 100x our recorded amount (for example, pmt_000231 is $19.32 in our records but $1,932.00 at the provider). That breaks payments_match_provider. The ledger books the provider's amounts from webhooks, so ledger_balanced and matches_provider still pass, but our payment records disagree with the provider. One payment (pmt_000233) is still pending on our side but already charged at the provider. That is likely in-flight timing, though it may also be a side effect of the unit change. Charges before pmt_000231 match. What remains open: I did not confirm the outbound request body in logs or traces, and the deploy log does not show the setting's value before this deploy.

evidence.shows: payments_match_provider fails with 59 findings starting at pmt_000231. Each provider charge is exactly 100x our amount_cents (1932 vs 193200, 14312 vs 1431200, and so on). The other four invariants pass, so the damage is limited to charge amounts.
payments-api was redeployed at 16:57:59Z, about 17s before the alert, with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. It is the only service changed after the 16:56:32Z stack start.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll payments-api back to its pre-16:57:59Z settings so charge amounts are sent in the unit the provider expects. Then refund or adjust with the provider the excess on the roughly 59 overcharged payments from pmt_000231 onward. Correct the ledger, which booked the inflated amounts, through a data repair. Resolve pmt_000233's pending state.

diagnosis.blast_radius: payments-api pauses while its container is recreated, so payment and refund requests fail or retry for a few seconds. The rollback does not repair the charges already inflated at the provider or the ledger entries booked from them. Those need a separate refund and data repair. Synthetic data only.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes things worse, redeploy payments-api with the 16:57:59Z settings (CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars, PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, REFUND_CONNECTION=returned). Then rerun the money check to confirm which state is correct.
